_meta.purpose: Reference manifest for the Living Document Workbench.

meta.title: Agent-Human Living Document
meta.subtitle: A browser-native review surface for asynchronous human-agent collaboration.
meta.thesis: A document becomes genuinely living when it lets humans review agent work at human speed: sections, annotations, proposals, media, changelogs, and worklogs remain separately addressable but visibly connected.
meta.audience: Researchers, product architects, prompt engineers, and coding agents maintaining complex evolving documents.

dashboard.focus: Demonstrate why chat and terminal scrollback are the wrong review surfaces for sustained agent work, and how a living document preserves human-paced review state.

health.label: Canonical content separation
health.detail: All section prose is stored in external Markdown files.

health.label: Decision clarity
health.detail: Three proposals remain intentionally unresolved for demonstration.

health.label: Accessible interaction
health.detail: Keyboard controls, high contrast, semantic landmarks, and reduced motion are included.

health.label: Canonical write path
health.detail: The portable starter exports change requests rather than writing source files directly.

metricDefinitions.label: Addressable sections
metricDefinitions.description: Canonical Markdown modules with stable IDs.

metricDefinitions.label: Open annotations
metricDefinitions.description: Questions, objections, decisions, and evidence attached to precise targets.

metricDefinitions.label: Local changes

sections.title: The temporal problem
sections.dek: Agents produce faster than humans can inspect, so the collaboration surface must decouple generation from review.

sections.title: Canonical content stays outside the shell
sections.dek: The interface renders a manifest and external Markdown instead of hiding the document inside application code.

sections.title: One document, several retrieval questions
sections.dek: Dashboard, reader, search, history, and changelog are distinct views because each answers a different question.

sections.title: Quick edits are visible overlays
sections.dek: Browser edits remain reversible and explicitly local until exported into a bounded source change.

sections.title: History, changelog, and worklog are not synonyms
sections.dek: Three ledgers preserve different kinds of memory and should remain separately queryable.

sections.title: Dark-first does not mean dark-only
sections.dek: Themes and microinteractions support reading and state recognition while remaining optional and accessible.

sections.title: Handoffs must be bounded and replayable
sections.dek: An agent receives explicit targets, constraints, evidence, decisions, expected files, and validation commands.

sections.title: The portable starter is a floor, not a ceiling
sections.dek: Server writes, collaboration, semantic indexing, and model execution belong in explicit extensions rather than hidden starter behavior.

proposals.title: Add a server-backed canonical save adapter
proposals.summary: Provide an optional authenticated Hono route with optimistic concurrency and schema validation while keeping the static export workflow intact.

proposals.title: Introduce paragraph-level anchors
proposals.summary: Generate stable paragraph anchors so annotations and agent requests can target passages more precisely than a whole section.

proposals.title: Add a semantic relationship graph
proposals.summary: Visualize dependencies, backlinks, proposals, and annotations as a navigable graph without replacing the section index.

proposals.title: Animate every section on scroll
proposals.summary: Apply entrance motion whenever a section reaches the viewport.

releases.title: Ongoing collaboration model added
releases.summary: The reference now supports skill-first conversations, model reply queues, selection annotations, resources, and format evolution guidance.

changes.text: Added dashboard, document, search, history, and changelog views around the human-paced review workflow.
Added local quick edits, undo, redo, annotations, proposal decisions, and change-request export.
Moved canonical prose from a monolithic JSON field into external Markdown files.
Added dark-first themes, a light paper theme, high contrast, motion preferences, and tactile control feedback.

releases.title: The maintenance contract
releases.summary: The initial skill established stable IDs, proposals, annotations, compatibility metadata, worklogs, and controlled agent handoffs.

changes.text: Defined the first living-document maintenance workflow and monolithic content model.

history.summary: Created the first maintenance skill and compatibility contract.
history.details: The original architecture used a single public/content.json file.

history.summary: Rejected dashboard sprawl, direct browser writes, and decorative motion.
history.details: The revised thesis preserved the requested features while separating editorial reading from operational controls.

history.summary: Migrated canonical section prose to external Markdown and introduced format 2.0.0.
history.details: Stable section IDs, proposals, annotations, and worklogs were preserved.

history.summary: Re-centered the package around the living-document raison d'etre and completed structural validation.
history.details: JavaScript syntax, JSON structure, source paths, IDs, relationships, themes, and exports were checked.

history.summary: Added format 2.1 collaboration fields for model replies and resources.
history.details: This is an additive schema revision. Existing format 2.0 documents can migrate by adding empty modelReplies and resources arrays.

worklogs.summary: Converted the skill into a contract-first living document package with a dark-first browser review surface, external Markdown, and safe local-edit workflow.
changed: Added format 2 schemas and migration guidance
Added dashboard, history, changelog, quick edit, search, themes, motion, and exports
Restored RAISON_DETRE.md as the first-class entry point for humans and agents
Added modelReplies and resources as first-class manifest collections
Added selection-based annotation support in the reference shell
suggested: Add an authenticated canonical write adapter only when a project has a server
Add paragraph-level IDs through an explicit schema migration
warnings: Visual interaction was designed and statically validated; browser automation is not bundled in the dependency-free starter
